title: Miley Cyrus Marries Maxx Morando in Intimate Palm Springs Wedding
excerpt: Miley Cyrus, 33, married Liily drummer Maxx Morando, 28, in an intimate poolside ceremony in Palm Springs on Saturday — a year after his Kyoto proposal.
content:
Miley Cyrus is married. The pop star, 33, and Liily drummer Maxx Morando, 28, said “I do” on Saturday, November 21, in an intimate ceremony at a private residence in Palm Springs, California, multiple sources confirm to PEOPLE. Entertainment Tonight was first to report the news.

Photos from the day show the ceremony took place beside the swimming pool, with Cyrus and Morando standing beneath an arch covered in white flowers. The ceremony was officiated by Flaming Lips frontman Wayne Coyne, according to Page Six.

The guest list stayed close to family. Cyrus’s mother, Tish Cyrus, and her sister, Noah Cyrus, were in attendance, and her father, Billy Ray Cyrus, attended with his girlfriend, actress Elizabeth Hurley. The couple posed for a family photo with Billy Ray, Hurley and Hurley’s son Damian Hurley.

A year after the Kyoto proposal

The wedding comes about a year after the couple got engaged. A source confirmed the engagement to PEOPLE on December 2, 2025, one day after Cyrus was spotted wearing a diamond ring at the Avatar: Fire and Ash world premiere in Los Angeles.

Morando proposed during a trip to Kyoto, Japan, in late 2025 — a place neither had visited before but both had long wanted to see. He told Wonderland magazine in July that he waited until the last day of the trip to ask, dropping to one knee in a garden at their hotel after coaxing Cyrus across a plank over a small pond.

Cyrus and Morando were first romantically linked in December 2021, photographed getting close backstage during her NBC holiday special, Miley’s New Year’s Eve Party, in Miami. They met on a blind date — “blind for me and not really for him,” Cyrus told British Vogue in 2023 — and were spotted kissing in West Hollywood by April 2022.

Small on purpose

The celebration matched how the couple have handled the relationship from the start: private and small. Cyrus told PEOPLE in December that keeping the engagement private was something she was astounded to have been able to do, adding that being older has made her “more protective of what I’m open to sharing.”

An exclusive source told PEOPLE in March that the pair envisioned a smaller and more meaningful wedding rather than a huge event — “not a big Hollywood production.”

The rehearsal dinner on Friday, November 20, followed the same script. Cyrus’s stepsister Lily-Rose Purcell shared photos from the dinner on Instagram Stories, including a menu topped with the couple’s initials, “M+M,” listing filet mignon, sherry cappuccino and hazelnut crème brûlée.

What it means

Analysis: For Cyrus, the wedding closes a five-year chapter that began in the glare of a New Year’s Eve broadcast and ends, deliberately, out of it. This is her second marriage; her first, to actor Liam Hemsworth, ended in divorce finalized in January 2020. The Palm Springs ceremony — family only, a musician friend officiating, no red carpet — reads as a statement of intent: the pop star who grew up in public is choosing, at 33, to keep the biggest moments for herself. Whether the newlyweds share more of the day themselves is the one detail still to come.
